newsitem.title: USA: CSCE coffee called to open up 8.00 to 10.00 cents.
newsitem.headline: CSCE coffee called to open up 8.00 to 10.00 cents.

text.p: CSCE coffee futures were called to open up 8.00 to 10.00 cents Thursday as traders expect this week's sizzling rally to continue after London robustas jumped nearly 14 percent overnight.
"We're going off London," said one trader. "They more than made their due.
"There's no reason to stop now," he added. "There was no selling yesterday, no selling the day before and there will probably be no selling today."

London robusta futures vaulted to 20-month highs early Thursday, on panicky roaster-led buying and talk of producer defaults in the Far East. LIFFE July soared $312 at the midday break, to $2,570, while September jumped $307, to $2,595.
Wednesday, New York arabica futures shot up for the second straight session, with July coffee soaring to a new 20-year high as speculators continued their buying frenzy.

July arabicas jumped to a new lifetime high of 297.00 cents a lb, the highest price since 1977, before closing at 295.55 cents, up a hefty 21.25 cents. Second-month September closed 19.20 cents higher at 256.70 cents, while the back months rose 6.00 to 12.60.
The July/September spread, a barometer of near-term supplies, widened to 38.85 cents from 36.80 cents at the close on Tuesday. September/December bulged to 42.15 cents from 35.55 cents on Tuesday.
After Wednesday's close, CSCE reported certified coffee stocks were unchanged, at 49,712 60-kg bags as of May 24. There was no coffee pending grading, the exchange said.

Also after the close, CSCE said it will raise the margin it will raise the margin on the July 1997 coffee "C" contract to $10,000, including a $4,000 spot charge, and the margin September 1997 coffee "C" contract will increase to $8,000, including a $2,000 spot charge, effective today.
The margins on all other coffee contracts will increase by $1,000 to $6,000, CSCE said.
